items.title: Manuel "Fess" Manetta and Edward "Kid" Ory Interview, 1958-08-26
items.q: So finally, Papa Mudd dropped out. You know, you had to do your day job or you couldn't do the job. And I told him, it was best for him to try to hold one job.

ctx.x: It was Ory and Oliver's jazz band. I was leading the band.

Yeah. With my band, I just, the way it happened that Oliver used to come around where we played at Lincoln Park and St. Catherine Hall and various places he was working. And so he said, why, why don't you give him a chance sometime? I said, well, when you get good enough. But I'm trying. I said, okay. So finally, Papa Mudd dropped out. You know, you had to do your day job or you couldn't do the job. And I told him, it was best for him to try to hold one job. If you want the other job, I'll have to get someone…
Was Oliver about the same age as you or was he a little older?

items.title: Edward "Kid" Ory Interview, 1957-04-20
items.q: Papa Mudd was with me then. Papa Mudd was playing trumpet.

ctx.x: Yeah, my band was right in front of it. I heard a trumpet back there.
Was it, this is a little later, or about the same time as? Well. Oh, that was... A few years later? Around 1912, wasn't it? Papa Mudd was with me then. Papa Mudd was playing trumpet.

items.title: Edward "Kid" Ory Interview, 1957-04-20
items.q: And gave Titty Girl and another? Another one. They were always trying to be leaders. So I gave them a band.

ctx.x: What made you go to Chicago? I don't want to see the country. I had to work. I was waiting for a man at this band.

He gave away two of his bands? I gave Papa Mudman a band. One of them? And gave Titty Girl and another? Another one. They were always trying to be leaders. So I gave them a band. They never did do nothing. He came home and found them starving when he came back to the west coast. So.
Give them a job again. You went there in 25. What did you do when you got to Chicago? Had you ever played in Chicago before that? No.
